- Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then decline too sharply, missing sustained upward trends.
- Model underestimates prices during periods of strong upward momentum (e.g., 70–75 range) and overestimates during consolidation or downward phases.
- Forecasts show a lag in responding to recent price drops — model holds higher values longer than actuals.
- Mean reversion is overemphasized — model prematurely assumes prices will return to prior levels after spikes.
- Overshoot after spikes is common — model forecasts peak higher than true outcome, especially in the 3rd–5th day after a spike.
- Model fails to capture the “tail” of a trend — underestimates late-period price corrections or rebounds.
- Forecasts are overly sensitive to recent volatility — model reacts too strongly to short-term noise, leading to erratic adjustments.
